title: Reverse-and-add in base 2 shows localized structures and never repeats

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Reverse-and-add in base 2 shows localized structures and never repeats

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The base-2 reverse-and-add process (add a number to its digit-reversal) started from 512 produces localized structures like those in cellular automata, and its overall pattern never appears to become simply repetitive.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Localized structures are visible, but the overall pattern never seems to take on any kind of simple repetitive form.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 4, “Systems Based on Numbers”; section “Elementary Arithmetic” (from p. 117), p. 126. Scope: base-2 reverse-and-add iteration from particular starting numbers

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch04-07: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.83

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The exact process is cheap to reproduce and its finite pattern can be independently analyzed. Current finite computation can support the observation but does not by itself resolve its asymptotic wording.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reproduce base-2 reverse-and-add from 512, quantify spatially persistent local motifs, and search the exact trajectory for eventual periodicity over a long horizon. The visible-structure claim is directly checkable, while a proof of eventual periodicity or nonperiodicity is needed for the unbounded repetition claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Finite absence of repetition cannot prove never-repetitive behavior.

Localized structure needs a declared detector.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.7
data existence: 0.92
discriminating power: 0.78
operationalizability: 0.8
analysis feasibility: 0.94

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The process and the seed 512 are fixed, and Wolfram already displays the millionth step, which is reproducible with ordinary big-integer code. That decides whether localized structures and the absence of short repetition survive much longer inspection. It does not decide the universal claim that the pattern never becomes simply repetitive, so the existing computation resolves a long but finite part of the statement.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Iterate base-2 reverse-and-add from 512 for a very large number of steps, detect persistent localized blocks by spatial correlation, and test the digit field for an eventual global period. Onset of simple repetition would refute the claim; persistence of localized structures without a short period supports it on that horizon.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A trajectory that is not periodic in any feasible prefix can still become periodic later, so 'never' is not finitely settled.

Localized structures can be defined in more than one way, and some definitions will count transient clumps.

fields.label: Dimension scores

discriminating power: 0.6
analysis feasibility: 0.75
